To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the use of nonclinical and in silico data can help identify potential adverse drug reactions in humans; (ii) the use of clinical data can help identify the mechanism of action and potential safety signals of a drug; (iii) the use of both nonclinical and clinical information together can help identify potential drug–drug interactions; and (iv) the use of all three data types can help identify the patient populations most likely to experience adverse drug reactions.
the integration of nonclinical and early clinical drug safety data can be used to create a ‘life-cycle’ system that will reduce the number of drugs that fail due to adverse reactions in patients.
the fusion of non-clinical and clinical data to identify and predict human drug safety is a major goal for the pharmaceutical industry, government regulatory agencies and healthcare systems.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the mechanisms underlying adverse drug reactions and their incorporation into the design and development process of new therapeutics.
the identification, development, and validation of new biomarkers for the early detection of human adverse drug reactions and the development of new approaches to drug design.
understanding how the molecular basis of drug safety can be integrated with the molecular basis of efficacy, and how this knowledge can be used to predict drug safety in humans.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the field of pharmacosafety is now poised to become a major player in the drug discovery and development process.
the future for drug safety is very promising and the next few years should witness a major change in how we think about and approach this important aspect of drug research and development.
a fusion of nonclinical, clinical and postmarketing data is essential in predicting and possibly eliminating adverse drug reactions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a new approach is emerging in which nonclinical and clinical drug safety data are integrated to provide a better understanding of the safety of drugs in humans.
the future will be based on a fusion of clinical and nonclinical data to develop a more accurate and predictive understanding of drug safety.
the fusion of non-clinical and clinical data is a key element in the development of a translational science approach to drug safety.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the fusion of non-clinical and clinical data is critical to the development of safe drugs and the elimination of adverse drug reactions.
a fusion of nonclinical data with clinical data can be used to predict human drug-induced liver injury (DILI).
the integration of nonclinical and early phase clinical data is essential to the success of the drug development process.
